compile.nuance: Catch-all 'have all underwriting closing conditions been met' bundle: option 'UW Condition-A' is a residual bucket for any unmet condition and does not enumerate a fixed guide-checkable set (UW closing conditions are loan-file-specific stipulations, not a closed list); D1-3-02 governs the general QC review-of-approval-conditions obligation. Only the 4506-C sub-item (UW-Conditions-2) has a direct, specific guide anchor (B3-3.1-02: signed IRS Form 4506-C required per borrower at or before closing). The letter-of-explanation sub-item (UW-Conditions-1) has no dedicated guide section — grepped 'letter of explanation'/'LOE' across guide/sections/ with zero hits — it is covered only by the D1-3-02 umbrella. Decomposition required to separate the two guide-specific children from the un-enumerable residual bucket.

compile.nuance: The Insured Closing Protection Letter (ICPL/CPL) is an ALTA/title-industry closing artifact not named verbatim anywhere in the guide corpus (grepped 'ICPL', 'closing protection letter' — zero hits); B7-2-01/B7-2-02 are cited as the governing acceptable-title-insurer requirement the ICPL operationalizes, and D1-3-02 as the general closing-documentation-consistency anchor for the borrower-info-match option. The 'mortgagee clause' option is atypical for a CPL (mortgagee clauses attach to hazard/flood policies per B7-3-07, not closing protection letters); B7-3-07 is the only guide section defining mortgagee-clause requirements and is cited for that option despite the card-subject mismatch — flagged as a base-data naming oddity, not a compile defect.

question_text: (Best Practice) Were all Limited English Proficiency (LEP) requirements met?

defect_options.response: (Best Practice) Standard/approved translated docs not issued based on the applicant(s) LEP pref.

finding.description: (Best Practice) Standard and approved translated documents were not issued to the applicant(s) in their preferred language.

compile.nuance: (Best Practice)/O-CFPB-prefixed: Limited English Proficiency translated-document issuance is a CFPB fair-lending best practice, not a Fannie Mae Selling Guide requirement. Exhaustive grep for 'Limited English Proficiency', 'LEP', 'translat', 'language preference', 'preferred language' across guide/sections/ surfaces only foreign-origin income/asset document translation rules (B3-3.2-02, B3-4.3-01, B3-5.2-01, B3-4.2-05, B3-5.1-02), which govern translating borrower-provided foreign documents to English — not applicant-LEP-preference-based disclosure issuance at closing. No Selling Guide basis exists.

question_text: Were all ECOA closing requirements met?

defect_options.response: No, a copy of the appraisal was not provided promptly, or three business days prior to closing

finding.description: Copies of each appraisal or written valuation were not provided to the applicant promptly upon completion, or three business days prior to consummation of the transaction (for closed-end credit) or account opening (for open-end credit), whichever is earlier.

defect_options.response: No, a signed appraisal delivery waiver was not obtained at least 3 business days prior to closing

finding.description: The applicant's waiver of appraisal delivery was not obtained at least three business days prior to consummation.

compile.nuance: The ECOA/Reg B appraisal-copy-delivery timing rule (copy provided promptly upon completion or ≥ 3 business days before consummation; or a signed waiver ≥ 3 business days before consummation) is a CFPB regulation, not a Fannie Mae Selling Guide-authored requirement. A3-2-01 (Compliance With Laws) is cited as the general seller/servicer obligation to comply with ECOA and related regulations — it names ECOA explicitly but does not detail the 3-business-day appraisal-delivery mechanics. Grepped 'three business days'/'3 business days' across guide/sections/ — no ECOA-appraisal-delivery-specific match found anywhere in the corpus.

The 3 options fully enumerate the section's requirement set (reason, documentation, loan-limit compliance on modification/recast), so no decomposition. No literal duplicate options.
